cohort_definition: Two Sigma entry-level cohorts, kept separate: (a) Quantitative Researcher interns and full-time campus hires, (b) Software Engineering interns and full-time campus hires, and (c) the New Seekers Summit early-exposure program for first- and second-year undergraduates. Internships are 10 weeks, summer, New York (Soho) per official postings.
sample_size_note: No licensed population sample used. Curated-qualitative CIR from public sources only (Doc 3 §1.6 Phase 1); no cohort percentages are stated because none were sourced.

data_sources.claim: Two Sigma official Quantitative Researcher Internship (2027 Summer) posting
Two Sigma official Software Engineering Internship (Summer 2027) posting
Two Sigma official internships page, including eligibility by role family
Two Sigma official article on the New Seekers Summit for first- and second-year undergraduates interested in quantitative research and data science

school_dist.claim: Two Sigma publishes no school distribution for these cohorts. Omitted rather than estimated.

prior_employer_dist.claim: Firm-stated on the QR intern posting: no finance background is required, and more than half of Two Sigma's employees come from outside the finance industry (firm's own wording in the posting).

major_dist.claim: QR interns: pursuing a degree in a technical or quantitative discipline — statistics, mathematics, physics, electrical engineering or computer science — with approximately one year remaining, all levels from bachelor's to doctorate (official posting).
Engineering interns: undergraduates entering junior or senior year, master's students and PhDs in a technical or quantitative field (official internships page).

skills_dist.claim: QR: intermediate skill in at least one programming language (C, C++, Java or Python named), an in-depth research project on real-world data, and clear communication of complex ideas.

SWE: the posting describes engineers who focus on analysis, experimentation, design and elegant implementation, building scalable tools for data exploration; the firm says it values curiosity and insight balanced with pragmatism.

path_patterns.pattern: New Seekers Summit (first/second year) -> QR internship -> full-time quantitative researcher (the firm's own profile follows one student through exactly this sequence: summit, interview, internship, full-time role)

10-week summer internship (QR or SWE) with an assigned mentor and a single project ending in a final presentation -> full-time campus hire (separate campus full-time postings exist for both QR and SWE)

entry_routes.route: Quantitative Researcher Internship (2027 Summer, 10 weeks, New York)
entry_routes.who_it_fits: Students with about one year left in a technical/quantitative degree, bachelor's through doctorate, with a real-data research project

entry_routes.route: Software Engineering Internship (Summer 2027, 10 weeks, New York)
entry_routes.who_it_fits: Juniors/seniors, master's and PhD students in technical or quantitative fields

entry_routes.route: Full-Time Campus Hire postings (QR and SWE)
entry_routes.who_it_fits: Final-year students and recent graduates applying directly to full-time roles
First- and second-year undergraduates curious about quantitative research/data science; no finance background required

hiring_bar_summary: The published bar is a quantitative degree in progress, real research or engineering substance, and intermediate-or-better coding — with finance knowledge explicitly treated as teachable. Unusually for this batch, the competition signal is firm-stated, but about its existing staff, not as an entry requirement: the official SWE intern posting notes the engineering group includes Putnam medalists, ACM programming competition finalists and International Mathematics Olympiad medalists. Read that as the caliber of colleagues the firm advertises, not as a checklist an applicant must match.

screening_signals.claim: QR posting: an in-depth research project examining real-world data is an explicit qualification — the single most concrete screen in the posting.
Independent thinking and the ability to creatively approach data analysis and communicate complex ideas clearly are explicit stated qualifications.
SWE posting: passion for data, curiosity and insight balanced with pragmatism and practicality are the firm's stated engineer signals.

process_stages.claim: No firm-published stage-by-stage interview process was included in the official postings/pages used; the internship structure itself is published (assigned mentor, single project, final presentation). Interview-stage detail from third-party sites was not treated as a firm fact and is omitted.

interview_styles.claim: The official internships page states the firm publishes interview tips from former interns ('Setting you up for success in your interviews'); specific question content is not published by the firm in sources used, so none is asserted.

values_culture_signals.claim: Scientific method applied to markets: the firm describes a rigorous, collaborative, scientific approach, hypothesis testing, and learning from academic research (reading circles and seminars are named intern activities in the QR posting).

hiring_cadence: Summer-cycle based: 10-week internships in the summer at the New York (Soho) office; 2027 Summer postings for both QR and SWE internships were live on the official careers site at verification (October 2026). New Seekers Summit is an annual one-day virtual program. Exact application deadlines are set per posting and must be checked on the live posting each cycle.

compensation_notes.note: No compensation figure is stated: sampled official Two Sigma intern postings did not publish a salary range in the text retrieved.

referral_weight_notes: No firm-published statement on referral weight was found in sources used.
red_flags: Do not read the firm's staff-caliber line (Putnam/IMO/ACM medalists among engineers) as an application requirement — the posting's actual qualifications are degree, coding and research/engineering substance.
Third-party 'interview guide' pages for Two Sigma SWE are mostly content-farm material and contradict each other; only the firm's pages were used here.
QR eligibility is time-boxed (approximately one year remaining in the program); applying in the wrong year wastes the attempt.
thesis_text: Bottom line: Two Sigma is the most research-shaped door in this batch. Its own postings define the successful profile plainly: a technical or quantitative degree in progress (statistics, math, physics, electrical engineering, computer science), intermediate coding in a mainstream language, and — the distinctive screen — an in-depth research project on real-world data that you can explain clearly. The firm explicitly says finance is not required and that more than half its employees come from outside finance; it teaches the market part to people who bring the science part. Routes in, ranked: (1) the 10-week QR internship if you have the research project, timed to the year you have roughly one year of your program left; (2) the parallel SWE internship or full-time campus hire if your strength is building scalable data systems — a genuinely separate cohort, not a consolation prize; (3) for freshmen and sophomores, the New Seekers Summit, which the firm's own profile shows feeding the internship-to-full-time path. The culture signal to match is scientific: hypotheses, experiments, reading the literature, and a final presentation of one deep project rather than a pile of shallow ones.
known_biases_of_data: Built only from public firm pages, official postings and credible public reporting. No LinkedIn or logged-in data (Doc 3 §1.1). Firm-published program statistics are marketing-adjacent and self-reported; interview details from candidate-report sites are anecdotal and labeled as such. Survivorship bias applies: sources describe who is hired, not who applied and failed.
